genericProblem: A governance account page can appear functional while it filters or sorts facts outside the owner, combines separate assignments into one false match, or labels invitation/audit/update data as authentication history.
finiteDenominator: platform account query contract and generated client
WorkspaceUserService platform count and page-ID predicates
platform account edge mapper and session boundary
counterexamples: Invitation/public mobile stays masked although authenticated platform account mobile is plain.
Operations-admin invitation tabs remain separate consumers.
Platform super-admin authorization is not a workspace capability mapping.

findings.evidence: Account UI disables standard search and owner page lacks type/ref filters.
findings.minimumFix: owner-backed query contract and ProTable QueryFilter state.

findings.evidence: Platform page joins role assignments and maps lastLoginAt absent.
findings.minimumFix: same-assignment EXISTS plus owner authentication fact.

findings.evidence: Assignment/role UI joins values into one string.
Platform invitation pagination treated an absent sorter as a sort transition and reset the requested page.
findings.minimumFix: guard page reset by sorter.order; use a Card header for task explanation/action and a labelled existing public invitation-page link.

findings.evidence: A type-only invitation filter can look healthy when its fixture has only one type or the browser proof asserts only a 200 response; neither proves that nonmatching assignment intents are excluded.
findings.minimumFix: owner proof creates competing types and asserts exclusion; L2 reads the type-only owner page and asserts every returned item has the selected type.

findings.evidence: Invitation creation accepted mixed target type/ref intents even though public and management presentation require one target; the resulting validly persisted record became unrenderable and polluted later list reads.
findings.minimumFix: owner create validates a single target type and ref before the first persistence write; the same-intent read predicate keeps an explicit malformed-row counterexample.
